user_text: Perfect, that's done. Wow, it's really late.
text:
It really is — 2 PM on a Thursday doesn't *sound* late, but if you've been deep in unit planning mode, it sure *feels* late! 😄

You've got a solid genetics unit now — clear goals, NGSS alignment, and assessments that actually ask students to *think*. That's a lot of heavy lifting done in one sitting.

When you come back to it fresh, a couple of things worth eyeballing:

- **The chi-square piece in Assessment 2** — make sure your students have had enough practice with it before it shows up on a graded task. It tends to be a bottleneck.
- **The policy brief rubric** — drafting that early in Week 3 gives you time to norm expectations with students before they write.

But that's future-you's problem. Go rest, recharge, and enjoy the fact that your three weeks are mapped out. Nice work! 🎉
